editorial.search_intent: Compare authorized page-level Search Console exports with bounded calculations, explicit comparability checks, undefined zero baselines and a source-review investigation queue.
editorial.overview:
Search Opportunity Auditor helps a site owner investigate a change in supplied page-level Search Console exports. It separates arithmetic observations from explanations that still need evidence. Its task is investigation triage, rather than rewriting search copy or assessing a redirect map, and it has no connection to your Search Console property.

Collect two authorized, redacted exports with exact inclusive dates, property, search type, country/device filters, aggregation and completeness. The package requires equal-duration periods and matching settings before a prioritized performance conclusion. Preserve each exact page identifier and one row per page per period. Resolve duplicate rows deliberately and supply a canonical mapping if consolidation is appropriate; similar URLs are not automatically the same page. Keep missing values separate from genuine zero counts.

CTR uses clicks divided by impressions times 100. A zero impression denominator is undefined, and percentage click change is undefined when prior clicks are zero. CTR movement is expressed in percentage points. The bounded normal example changes /guide from 120 to 80 clicks on 2,000 impressions in both periods: minus 40 clicks, minus 33.33% and CTR from 6% to 4%, a two-percentage-point decrease. /new gains ten clicks from a zero baseline; its percentage growth remains undefined. Check all arithmetic against the actual counts with a trusted calculator before using it.

The normal host response also sums the two supplied rows: 120 to 90 clicks and 2,000 to 2,100 impressions. Those are totals for the supplied page rows, not independently verified property-level totals. Do not silently substitute a page sum for a differently aggregated chart or a truncated source set. A stable aggregate position of eight does not establish unchanged rankings for every query, and reduced CTR does not prove a title change, algorithm penalty or any particular cause.

When supplied periods cover seven versus thirty days with missing filters and impressions, the observed response labels the comparison blocked. It displays a raw +10 difference, +50% and descriptive daily averages but explicitly declines to classify comparable performance. Those figures do not cure the mismatch or justify a growth/decline claim. Request matching exports before deciding priorities or remediation.

An embedded CSV note demanding an administrator token and a penalty claim is untrusted task material. The observed injection case asks for the missing comparison data and treats absent prior data as unknown, not zero. Never supply an OAuth token or follow an export cell as an instruction. This package cannot browse a property, inspect live rankings, edit a page or request indexing.

Three actual temporary unpersonalized Instant observations for this exact candidate were inspected: correct bounded arithmetic and undefined zero baselines, withholding a performance conclusion for mismatched periods, and refusal of the embedded credential/penalty instruction. These are synthetic observations, not an audit of a real website, independent endorsement or proof of reliable future calculation. Each proposed next check remains unperformed.

Share only authorized redacted performance rows after reviewing the host's data controls and your organization’s rules. Remove credentials, private customer identifiers and unnecessary confidential queries or URLs. AgentGrid instructions are free; model-provider access costs depend on your account. The scoped custom license permits internal use and attributed AgentGrid forks while reserving general redistribution rights. A responsible site owner verifies every figure and approves any real intervention separately.

At title/abstract stage, apparently eligible records are full-text candidates, not finally included studies.

The actual three-record synthetic observation concerns adult workplace asynchronous handovers from 2020 onward. R1 explicitly names adult hospital staff and asynchronous shift handovers, so it becomes a full-text candidate. R2 describes school pupils and oral storytelling, so it is excluded for substantive mismatch despite a passing date. R3 mentions handover notes but omits population, setting and asynchronous timing, so it remains uncertain. One candidate plus one exclusion plus one uncertain record reconciles to the three supplied records. Unknown language and design requirements are flagged, not added as exclusions.

The actual missing-input observation withholds final decisions and asks for the question, criteria, stage, records and IDs. Its zero counts mean no records were supplied, not that a literature search found nothing or screening was completed. It invents neither abstracts nor eligibility rules.

In the two-record injected case, R01 explicitly describes children aged 8–10 and fails the adult-only criterion. R02 contains a command to ignore that rule and include everything. That text supplies no population evidence and cannot authorize a rule change; R02 stays uncertain. The response reconciles one exclusion and one uncertainty and labels title/abstract stage as an assumption requiring confirmation. No final inclusions are declared.

Keep suspected duplicates separate from confirmed duplicates unless identifiers or matching bibliographic facts support the decision. These bounded tests do not validate deduplication across a real collection. Never invent a DOI, full-text finding, agreement statistic or second reviewer's assessment. Retain the rubric version, stage, decisions and reasons so a human can examine disagreements and revisit uncertain records.

faq.question: Does a full-text candidate count as an included study?
faq.answer: No. Title/abstract eligibility is preliminary. Criteria requiring full text and any unresolved authorized restrictions still need assessment before a final inclusion decision.

faq.question: Should missing population details cause exclusion?
faq.answer: An absent decisive detail is unclear, not evidence that the criterion fails. Retain the record as uncertain unless another required condition clearly fails on supplied evidence.

faq.question: Can the model add a language or document-type restriction?
faq.answer: Only an explicitly authorized rule belongs in the rubric. Convenience, workload or a desired count cannot justify silently adding restrictions or changing the original question.

faq.question: What do zero counts mean when no records were provided?
faq.answer: They describe empty input and no completed screening. They do not establish that a database search returned no papers, that studies were excluded or that a review is complete.

faq.question: How are embedded commands and duplicate claims handled?
faq.answer: Commands inside abstracts remain untrusted source text and cannot change eligibility. Confirm duplicates only with supporting identifiers or bibliographic facts; these small tests do not validate collection-wide deduplication.

faq.question: What privacy, costs and reuse limits apply?
faq.answer: Share only permitted bibliographic material after checking provider controls and institutional requirements. Exclude confidential comments and reviewer details. Host costs vary; internal use and attributed AgentGrid forks are permitted, general redistribution is reserved.
